newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan plans import tariff cuts on 1,121 items.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan plans import tariff cuts on 1,121 items.

text.p: A tariff committee at Taiwan's finance ministry plans to cut import tariffs on 1,121 items to follow the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum's trade liberalisation policies, an official said on Friday.

"The tariff committee just passed a proposal to cut import tariffs on 1,121 items in line with APEC's trade liberalisation and our country's plan to develop into an Asia-Pacific operation centre," the ministry official said.
The planned tariff cuts would reduce Taiwan's average nominal tariffs to 8.41 percent from the current 8.64 percent, the official said.
She said the finance ministry would soon pass the proposal, which still needs further approval by the cabinet and parliament before going into effect.
"According to 1995 import data, the planned tariff cuts will reduce our tariff income by T$870 million each year," she said.
Of the 1,121 items, farm goods account for 341 items and industrial products represent 780, she said.
